concept.name: Margin
concept.definition: Collateral or account equity required to support leveraged positions or credit exposure, rather than the full notional value of the position.
concept.intuition: It links the capital posted by a trader to the larger exposure and credit risk carried in the account.
concept.mechanics: The broker or clearinghouse values positions and collateral, applies current requirements, posts gains and losses, and demands more collateral or liquidates when equity is insufficient.
concept.failure_modes: House requirements can rise without notice, prices can gap, and forced liquidation or interest can make losses exceed the initial capital posted.
concept.misconceptions: Margin is collateral or account equity, not a fixed maximum loss; leverage magnifies gains and losses on the trader's equity.
concept.example: Posting $5,000 to support $10,000 of margin stock leaves a $5,000 broker loan and exposes the investor to the full price movement.
